models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
models.role: Route exhaustion & conjecture mining — the main 24/7 reasoner
models.runtime: llama.cpp on the V100 box; vLLM pipeline-parallel across 2 nodes
models.notes: 13B active params = ~8 GB read per token: MoE geometry that makes cheap VRAM fast. 1M context for whole-route prompts.

models.name: Goedel-Prover-V2 32B
models.runtime: vLLM, one instance per 3090, batched tactic search
models.notes: Near-frontier formal proving from a 32B model; every output kernel-verified.

models.name: DeepSeek-Prover-V2 7B
models.role: Lean proof search — wide cheap swarm
models.runtime: vLLM, many parallel streams per GPU

models.name: Qwen3.6 Coder (MoE)
models.role: Numerics code-gen — CUDA kernels, arb/MPFR pipelines, experiment harnesses

models.name: Qwen3.5 small + embeddings
models.role: Triage, dedup, result classification, similarity search over findings

models.name: Qwen3.5 32B (reasoning)
models.role: Interactive testbench — the model to use TODAY on a single 24 GB GPU while ALAN is built
models.runtime: vLLM or llama.cpp, fully VRAM-resident — never offload
models.notes: Replaces qwen2.5-math:72b in current tests: a 72B dense model on a 24 GB card offloads to CPU and crawls; a 32B reasoning model fully resident is 10-50x faster and actually explores.

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.role: Big gun — overnight verdicts on the hardest surviving routes
models.runtime: llama.cpp RPC spanning fleet + V100 box; single-digit tok/s
models.notes: Current open-weight intelligence leader. Slow across the network — an overnight machine, not a chat partner.

models.name: Aristotle (Harmonic)
models.role: Lean 4 proof completion — submit files with open sorries, get kernel-verified completions
models.costNote: free for now — $0 cloud exception; local prover swarm is the sovereign fallback if pricing changes
models.notes: IMO gold-equivalent (2025) with machine-verifiable Lean output. Route the hardest sorries here first while it costs nothing.

models.name: Claude Fable 5 / Opus 5 (batch)
models.role: Rigor layer — proof planning, §-level audits, avenue triage
models.costNote: paid — a few hundred to ~$2k/month; only survivors from the local layers reach it

layers.name: 1 · Orchestrator — the route runner
layers.purpose: Pulls avenues from the improvement queue, fans experiments out across the serving layers, collects results, promotes survivors upward. The only custom software in the stack.

layers.name: 2 · Model gateway
layers.purpose: One endpoint for every model — local vLLM backends, llama.cpp, Aristotle, and the frontier API all behind the same interface, with per-avenue token accounting. Swapping a model is a config edit.

layers.name: 3 · Batch serving
layers.purpose: Continuous batching for the prover swarm, coder, and triage models. Ampere has no FP8 — INT4 Marlin is the format.

layers.name: 4 · Big-model serving
layers.tech: llama.cpp (GGUF; RPC mode to span machines)
layers.purpose: Hosts DeepSeek V4 Flash fully in 256 GB of NVLinked HBM; RPC-spans the whole cluster for GLM-5.3 overnight runs. GGUF needs no BF16, so Volta's software sunset doesn't bite.

layers.name: 5 · Formal proving
layers.tech: Lean 4 + mathlib kernel checks; Aristotle API for the hardest sorries
layers.runsOn: EPYC cores (kernel) + prover swarm (layer 3) + Harmonic cloud (free)
layers.purpose: Every candidate proof is machine-checked — hallucination-proof by construction. Local swarm generates; the kernel judges; Aristotle closes what the swarm can't.

layers.name: 6 · Verified numerics
layers.runsOn: V100 box (62 TFLOPS FP64) + EPYC cores
layers.purpose: Λ-bound and H_t corridor-certificate campaigns produce rigorous intervals, not floats. The reason the V100 box is in the BOM.

layers.name: 7 · State & telemetry
layers.tech: Postgres results store; nvidia-smi + IPMI exporters
layers.purpose: Every experiment, proof, and certificate lands in one queryable store; exporters feed cluster-state.json and the Mission Control page. Thermal alarms pause the queue before hardware sees a critical temp.

pipelines.title: Falsify-first conjecture mill

stages.step: Propose candidate identities, inequalities, or structures from a route card
stages.who: DeepSeek V4 Flash, N parallel samples at diverse temperatures

stages.step: Implement each candidate as executable code (mpmath/Sage/CUDA)
Execute against zero datasets and known constraints — try hard to break it
Triage survivors: dedup by embedding, cluster, rank by surprise
Promote the top handful for deep review

pipelines.verifier: numerical execution — a conjecture that fails once is dead, no debate
pipelines.output: a nightly ledger of surviving candidates with evidence attached

pipelines.title: Lean formalization treadmill

stages.step: Autoformalize route statements and lemma targets into Lean 4
Tree-search proofs: pass@64 tactic candidates per open goal
stages.who: Goedel-Prover 32B + Prover 7B swarm on the 3090 fleet

stages.step: Ship the stuck sorries out for completion
Merge verified lemmas into the route's formal library

pipelines.verifier: the Lean kernel — hallucination is structurally impossible
pipelines.output: a growing mathlib-style library of machine-verified lemmas per route

pipelines.title: FP64 certificate factory

stages.step: Spec an interval computation from a route card (Λ bounds, corridor checks)
Write the arb/MPFR or CUDA FP64 kernel

pipelines.verifier: interval arithmetic — outputs are rigorous enclosures, not floats
pipelines.output: certificate artifacts citable in a paper

pipelines.title: Overnight verdict

stages.step: Batch the hardest stuck questions with full route context (1M tokens)
Deep single-stream reasoning runs while the house sleeps
stages.who: GLM-5.3 spanned across everything, or frontier batch API

stages.step: Structured verdicts land in the morning review queue

pipelines.verifier: human — this is the one pipeline whose output is judgment, not artifacts
pipelines.output: morning briefing: kill / pivot / escalate per route

rules.rule: Never trust prose math — only artifacts
rules.why: A model saying 'this holds' is noise. Code that ran, a proof the kernel checked, an interval that closed — those are signal. Every pipeline ends in a verifier that is not an LLM.

One smart sample loses to 64 diverse samples plus a ruthless verifier. Budget pass@N per goal, not conversations. This is why instruct-tuned math models (qwen2.5-math-72b) feel dead: they compress toward one answer instead of fanning out.

A 72B dense model at Q4 is ~43 GB; on a 24 GB card the runtime silently offloads to CPU and throughput collapses 10-50x. On one 3090: 32B INT4 max. Big models only as MoE (V4 Flash: 284B total, 8 GB read per token) or on the V100 box.

rules.rule: Answer-machines answer; reasoners explore; provers prove
rules.why: Three different tools. Math-instruct models for lookups, reasoning models (V4 Flash class) for generation and conjecture, prover models for Lean. Using one for another's job wastes electricity.

rules.rule: The human files route cards, not prompts
rules.why: A route card = goal, known results, falsifiers to try, token budget. The orchestrator turns it into thousands of experiments. You review promoted survivors at breakfast, not chat logs at midnight.

rules.rule: vLLM for fleets, llama.cpp for giants, never Ollama defaults for research load
rules.why: Continuous batching is where the 50-200x cost advantage lives. Ollama is fine for kicking tires; the mill runs on vLLM with explicit quant, context, and batch settings.
